cell.label: Patient presents with "spider bite," pustular lesions, "boils" abscess (with tissue necrosis), cellulitis, impetigo, or infected wound.

Incise and drain abscess; if not performed, consider culture of draining wound, or aspirate or biopsy of central area of inflammation. Obtain culture and sensitivities (include "D-test" for clindamycin resistance if MRSA). Educate patient regarding infection control and wound care. Assess severity.

Outpatient management: Local care, I&D, ± topical antibiotics may be sufficient; oral antibiotics effective; beta-lactam antibiotics preferred for MSSA; if increased suspicion for MRSA based on presence of ≥1 risk factors, consider empiric therapy active against MRSA; adjust antibiotics based on results of culture & susceptibility testing; monitor response to therapy.
Febrile, appears ill, but no unstable comorbidities.

Outpatient management: Low suspicion for MRSA; beta-lactam antibiotics preferred for MSSA; if increased suspicion for MRSA based on presence of ≥1 risk factors, consider empiric therapy active against MRSA; adjust antibiotics based on results of culture & susceptibility testing; monitor response to therapy.
Appears toxic, unstable comorbidity, or limb-threatening infection; sepsis syndrome or life-threatening infection (e.g., necrotizing fasciitis).

Hospital management: Empiric broad-spectrum IV antibiotics including vancomycin for activity against S. aureus & MRSA; adjust therapy based on results of culture & susceptibility testing; monitor response to therapy; consult infectious disease specialist if no improvement or consider alternative agents (e.g., linezolid, daptomycin); switch to oral therapy based on susceptibility testing if: afebrile for 24 hours, clinically improved, able to take oral therapy, and close follow-up is possible.

footnotes.footnote: Beta-lactum antibiotics: include all penicillins & cephalosporins
